title: Rediscovering The Kingdom Change Mandate
paragraphs: Today I want to talk about the topic of the Kingdom’s leadership that is changing society, which is our main topic, but our focus today will be on rediscovering the Kingdom’s mandate for change. Please note that. Rediscovering the mandate for change in the Kingdom. I want to focus on understanding the task of transformation. The task of transformation. This is perhaps the most important series I have ever presented in my life regarding the application of the Kingdom's mandate to contemporary life.

This is a difficult series for me because it requires practical work. It requires interaction with the community. Most of the time, those who deal with spiritual issues seem to be more focused on the activity of the afterlife than on the practical, contemporary lifestyle. Therefore, this has been a very interactive experience for me so far. I have completed the entire series for next year. I've already finished it. I know what I need to cover and the instructions are very clear to me.

The Kingdom's leadership must change society now. If we don't do that, we will be victims of the transformation of others. So, I want to remind us what this series is about. The biggest challenge we face in our lives is the time we are living in now. I'm not sure if we all realize the nature of the times we are living in today. We are caught in a stream of convergence. Could you please write down this word? Convergence. Throughout history, you can study history.

I am talking about perhaps 5,000 or 6,000 years of history, and you will notice that history proceeded as usual until certain points where certain events began to occur. Now, there are always events happening in history. In fact, history is a record of events that take place. But there are certain points in history where certain things happen at the same time, which is unusual. This event is called convergence. They call it historical rapprochement.

If you study historical convergences, you will notice that life on planet Earth changed permanently during these convergences. We are entering one of these periods again. Convergence means that different forces that usually occurred separately began to occur at the same time. Therefore, the only thing we can expect to remain constant is change, because convergence changes everything. I call it the convergence current. It is similar to ocean currents that collide and create friction against each other.

I want you to write the word "current", please, because current is important. When my wife and I were in Brazil, we went on a private boat trip because our friends wanted us to see a meeting point. In Brazil, there is a place where the Amazon River, the largest river in South America, flows through the mountains, across countries and the Amazon rainforest, to empty into the ocean. So, you have fresh water, billions upon billions of enormous fresh water forces rushing through the Amazon River.

And it collides with the ocean, the Atlantic Ocean. So you have fresh water colliding with salt water. And you have mud that collides with clear sea water. One of the things I noticed before we got there was a constant disturbance. The boat was shaking and unstable. You couldn't even drop anchor. That was when the waters collided with the other waters. You have waters that collide with other waters. Both are water, but they are different, and the boat would not have remained stationary.

In fact, we had to hold on because the convergence of the two forces created currents that were not present anywhere else in either body of water. Then the second thing I noticed was that the color of that spot was different. The ocean was blue. The Amazon was almost brown or green, but the place was almost black because the mud that was hitting the fresh water stirred up ocean leaves and all sorts of debris and this black water. So, you have all this beautiful ocean and then these black waters.

When we got there, the man said, " This is the best place for fishing because the fresh water meets the salt water. It stirs up algae from the ocean so that fish from the Amazon and fish from the salt water come there to feed." Then the man said, "Now we must keep a good distance from the center because if we put the boat in the middle of it, the boat will sink down." It will turn over. We will die. He said, "The current there is very strong.

You have two currents colliding with each other and swirling around each other, forming something like a centrifuge that sucks things in. This is called a convergence. Historically, this is where we are now. And the currents are the dangerous part. Everyone say ' current affairs.' Currents. Look, this is dangerous. Say it slowly. Current affairs. There are some current affairs in your world, and they are strong currents. And those currents come and sweep you away with them.

And the only thing that doesn't move in the midst of this convergence is rock. Now, notice, if you get caught in the middle of this convergence, what happens to you? It pulls you in. Which means that even if you have an anchor —we had an anchor on the boat—the man said the anchor couldn't help us because an anchor needs a rock. So, wearing a life jacket doesn't protect you. Having an anchor doesn't protect you in the midst of this convergence. You need to find something that isn't part of this convergence.

You have to find a rock. Without a rock, the tide will sweep you away. Without a rock..." The currents will pull you in. And that's where we are right now. We have so many currents flowing at the same time that we're living through what I call a season of massive change. Can you take note? This isn't just an ordinary time to live in. This is a difficult time to live in. Some of you are feeling it. You turn on the television and are overwhelmed by the news. Every news channel is filled with so much confusion.

You have a woman being raped on a bus in India. Then you hear about hostages being shot, and there's no more room for negotiation. They're killing them. Then there are people strapping bombs to their bodies and blowing themselves up, killing 72 people. Then you have heads of state going to jail. You have bishops being accused of having relationships with boys. You have CEOs being considered criminals. There's so much going on.

It's a time when I want you to wake up, please, wake up to what's happening because you're going to spend the rest of your lives in this time. And we have three kinds of change that we need to focus on in this series, over the next few months. The first kind is personal change. The currents are hitting your life. Personality. The second change is institutional change. The systems that have been running the world are changing. Then there is national change, where countries are going through upheavals.

This includes, of course, not only culture but also politics and political systems. This is a fact. What do you do in the midst of this kind of convergence? 2013, I believe, marks the beginning of the convergence season. Everything will change. Change will be the greatest challenge of our time. The pace and nature of change will be so rapid that we won't be able to keep up. We are already feeling it. We will have to decide what changes we want.

I sat at my desk this week on more than one occasion, listening to the news from various sources, and I heard myself say: This is a crazy world. I'm not sure what's going to happen here, but we have to stand up and decide what's going to happen, or things will happen to us. So it's important that we decide what changes. We must know, understand, and define the changes that God wants. That's why God gave us the world, His church. Now, the power of change is astonishing. Let me address this very quickly.

Nothing is permanent. We know that. And change is constant. We also know that everything is changing and that change is inevitable. You can't stop it. Change is also the principle of life. We say that everything in life changes, and change is the principle of creation. Everything around us is going through a transitional phase, including this very meeting. The way this room was before you came in has changed. But here are some real things about change. Your body will change. Say amen.

Your relationships will change. Your friends will change. Your marriage will change. Your job will change. Your priorities will change. Even your values ​​will change. We have to be careful about this. Your knowledge base will change. Your interests will change. Then your children will change. Everything that affects your life will change, including your life itself. And there are four kinds of change that I've talked about, and I want to remind you of them quickly. There's change that we allow to happen.

There's change that we watch happen. Then there's change that we ask what happened because of. And there's change that we make happen. That's the kind we want to focus on. Now I want to remind you of something very serious. 2013 is the beginning of a season that I believe will last more than 10 years of radical transformation, and this will be a spiritual transformation. There will be a transformation Climate, environmental changes, and cultural changes too— we have to work through all of that.

We'll also see changes in the social structure, which I think we're already feeling coming to the Bahamas. Ah, all of us sitting here, and the millions who might be watching this program, you'll be going through all of those changes in your own countries. Look at them carefully. There will be a spiritual change. That means people will challenge their spiritual values. There will be climate changes. You'll find snow in places where it shouldn't be.

I think a few weeks ago, when I made that statement, someone called me and said, "It's snowing in Arizona." It has never snowed in Arizona before. At least not in the plains. "The climate will change. We will see environmental changes. Not just the physical environment, but also changes in the environment of your working conditions, labor relations, and political environments. And, of course, we will see changes in the social structure. There are 10 national changes I want you to remember.

I'll write them down quickly. These are important things. There will be political change. I don't know if I'm a prophet or what, but I know I can read the signs of the times. Politics will change. It has already begun. The politics that have effectively run countries for years will transform. Second, there will be constitutional changes. People will tamper with the established traditions of constitutional power. There will also be social change, and number four is very dangerous.

There will be ideological changes that produce your philosophy of life. This is dangerous. And I think that we, as most believers, sometimes become so vague that we become foolish. We must remember that people are constantly trying to tamper with our principles, and ideology is important to settle on. What are my principles? Because your ideology will determine your philosophy of life, which will determine the way you live and respond to life. There will also be changes..." Morality.

Morality will be under pressure. There will also be changes in values, and the two are linked. Whatever you value becomes your moral standard, which becomes your ethics. Religion will change. There will be many people undergoing religious conversions. Some will even abandon religion altogether. Most young people in our country, for example, are 14 years old. Many of them have never been to church. I know you can't believe that. But talk to Pastor Dave or a youth pastor.

He'll tell you he's shocked by the number of young people in the Bahamas who have never been to Sunday school. They grew up without ever going to church. Some of us in this room are used to church. So, we assume everyone has. And you may have listened to Brother Corey singing this morning and couldn't understand the words. You may not have liked his music. But let me tell you something. There are children who don't sing "Amazing Grace." They've never heard it.

And someone has to talk to those children in their own language. There will also be religious changes, and then scientific changes. And scientific change is dangerous. Absolutely, not just in the medical and pharmaceutical fields. We also recently heard that the North Korean leader has threatened the United States with a nuclear attack. This may seem trivial to you, but we cannot afford a war right now. He seems to be under pressure, being young. He's not even 30 yet. He's running an entire country.

There seems to be pressure on him from the older generation around him to prove himself. When someone is under pressure to prove themselves, they do irrational things. In other words, do n't sit there wondering whether this guy will push the button or not. I'm telling you now, if his threat becomes more intense this week, there will be some kind of reaction. And you haven't seen how your life will change yet. You think we have an economic problem. All we need right now is a war.

So there will be scientific changes where countries that didn't have nuclear weapons will acquire them. The Iranian president, you know, is fighting to gain control of nuclear energy. Don't just sit there and say " Hallelujah." These are serious matters. We need to know what's going on and how we're supposed to respond. Who knows, maybe it will lead me The journey to China eventually leads to North Korea, where I meet the right people and can save them. We don't know. To prevent war. Can God be that profound?

I have that kind of faith. There will also be technological changes. And here you are, holding an iPad in your hand right now. You prove it. But the last point is the one I want you to write in capital letters. There will also be changes in definitions. And that's a dangerous point. Changes in definitions. We live in a time where what used to be called bread is no longer bread. They're changing definitions. In other words, we've never in our lives debated what marriage is. We've never talked about it.

No civilization I've studied in history during my short life has ever argued about the definition of marriage. Not one. The Romans, the Greeks, the Byzantines—none of them argued about it. We're the only generation I know that sits down and redefines things. For example, we now call killing your child an abortion. It's actually murder because it's a human life. But we use nice words. We now call homosexuality nice things like a lifestyle. An alternative.

We use terms like preference, sexual preference, not deviance. Sexual preference. Deviance means you stray from the norm. But we don't want to call ourselves deviants. So we say we choose something as a preference. We redefine things. If a man is a man but wants to be like a woman, we have a new definition. We call him effeminate or a male feminist. There's no definition anywhere in the world for that. I do n't know. It doesn't exist. I've never seen "she" be a man. It doesn't make sense.

But they reinvent definitions. And that's important because they use definitions to manipulate your mind, to take away your conscience and conviction. You can't have conviction if I change the definition. For example, we call theft a white-collar crime. It's theft. People who tamper with records, we say they embezzled money. No, man, you lied and stole. But we use two new definitions. He's not a real criminal, you know. He's just been wayward since he was young. It's amazing how we've come to a time when no one...

Something's a clear definition. You can kill a man, and they can call it something else. They can say, you know, a temporary loss of control. A mental imbalance. You're a murderer, man. No, they say you were mentally unstable at the time. Then they say, maybe something went wrong with you when you were three. You were wetting the bed. Listen, man. You really are a murderer. But the way we're redefining things, you know? Look, don't just sit there when they hit you.

You better understand what they're hitting you with in the culture of this world. They call economic invasion another name. They call it shuttle diplomacy. They call it the IMF. It's economic invasion. Listen, don't get mad at me. That 's the reality. And we need to recognize that they're redefining some things. I remember when babies were coming out of the womb, the doctor would spank the baby. Like that. Now they say that's child abuse. Oh, I read that. I couldn't believe it; I was reading it in the magazine.

I said, wait a minute. How many babies have been spanked throughout history? Now that's abuse. The doctor can't hit him anymore. Oh, you'd better wake up. Now, when you punish your child as a form of discipline, that's called parental abuse. Definitions, Mommy used to say, "I'm going to discipline you." If you used that term today, they'd say you're violent. There are countries in the world where a child can sue their parents for disciplining them. I hope you're awake. Definitions are changing.

And throughout this series, we'll be talking about some of those definitions because they're confusing the concepts. This is the big conflict right now, which we'll go into more detail later, but it's the big conflict currently going on about the definition of marriage. People, you know, the conflict is about who decides what marriage means? Do we let a small group of 10% define marriage for us, or do we stand up and say, "No, find another name for that, but this isn't marriage"? What is the definition?

And these are the challenges we face. So, we live in an age of change. And I want to give you some of the terminology they use. I want you to write it down because you need to be smart enough to interpret what these phrases mean when You hear about it. I call it the age of redefinition. Some experts call this era by terms like "the new normal." Have you heard of that? Is there such a thing as the new normal? Of course, you have normal things, like a woman being a normal female.

And then now they have a new normal where a woman can be half, you know, whatever that means. So you have her being normal, but it's the new normal. That's the term they use, the new normal. Two men living together in a covenant that's called normal, but it's called the new normal. So they have a sitcom on TV now. It's called " Modern Family." You have to pay attention to those things. Your children are watching it. The modern family is two men with children on your television screen in your homes right now.

They call it the new normal. What is the new normal? Look, they're playing with words. They say it's normal for two women to get married. It's normal. It's just that you have the old normal. And we have the new normal. They say that's the new normal. That's not. How can that be normal? So we have to define the word " normal." And if normal is defined by nature, then there can't be a new normal. In other words, what is normal? Can you vote democratically to create something normal? No. Yes. They do.

They say if enough people vote for it, then they make it normal. How can you make something normal when it's unnatural? What is unnatural? Unnatural means against the norm. What is normal? Another term they use today is postmodernism. Have you ever heard of that? Postmodernism means that you all thought you were modern. But we're watching you now. You thought you were progressive. We've We've moved beyond evolution now. We're more complicated than the complicated ones. What kind of terminology do they use?

In other words, the Apostle Paul covered this in one sentence in Romans chapter 1. Paul says, "They invent new ways to sin." Can I quote it again? It's in Romans chapter 1. He said, " They invent new ways to sin." In other words, it's the same old sins, but they find new ways to do them. So, there's nothing new under the sun. It's just repackaging. And you live in a time when they come up with statements so fast you believe them. What about this? They say there's also an age of secular society.

Secularization of society. Secularization means they want to get rid of anything spiritual or religious in society. That's what secularization is called. Secularization is erasing any trace of religious, moral, or spiritual influence from society. And this is happening right now in the Bahamas. I think next week I'll show you what one of our MPs said in Parliament. I'm not going to start talking. I'm just going to show you the recording. I'm not going to say anything more about it.

I want you to You hear what's been said about secularizing the Bahamas in our parliament. That means getting rid of God. That's why they're arguing about the preamble. The preamble is problematic because it states that we respect Christian values. Christianity refers to spirituality, which is problematic for the secular mind. The secularist says: I don't want anything to bother my conscience. Leave my conscience alone. Let me decide what's acceptable and unacceptable. What's right and wrong. Let me decide that.

Forget this thing you call God. I am the end in myself. That's secularism. Another term they use, write it down, and it's a dangerous term. Enlightened society. Oh, that's a big term. It's a big term lately. You know, they say, "Well, you're not enlightened." I heard someone use it on a radio show the other day. A gay guy called in and said, "You know, some of these pastors aren't enlightened." They said they're not enlightened. What they mean is that your thinking is outdated. That's a dangerous statement.

Enlightened society means we're so liberal that we don't have Limits. The enlightened society says we are the law. The LINE society says we can change them whenever we want. Those are the laws. In the LINE society, we are so advanced now that we are able to accept anything we can personally justify, even if it's not inherently acceptable. If we can accept it ourselves, then it's acceptable. No limits. That's the society we're approaching. That's the mindset we're dealing with.

And please, as an individual, wake up, please, and think about this. Because when you go to work this week, there are people working next to you who think this way. They say things like, "You still believe in that ridiculous old book, the Bible, written by humans." That's old. That's outdated. That's obsolete. That's not an enlightened book. That's too old-fashioned. It doesn't keep up with the times. And they make you start questioning your own beliefs. It's called the enlightened society.

Every civilization that has claimed to be enlightened has destroyed itself. Yes, sir. Look at history. Yes, sir. Who do you think you are? Do you think you're Smarter than the Romans, the Egyptians, and the Greeks? They're all buried under the dust today. You can't think in a way that surpasses God. Listen, you'll never convince me that you're smarter than God. Never. And the laws He's made, you can't invent better laws than them. You can't even invent them. It's impossible to be more enlightened than light itself.

Yes, sir. Yes, sir. And God doesn't just give light. You know that He is the light. That means that if you don't have Him, what you call light is actually darkness. And Paul says that they call darkness light. And by the way, don't miss the next two sessions because you'll understand that light and darkness are at the heart of the conflict. We are enlightened. They say, " What do you mean two men ca n't get married? You're not enlightened. Someone has to challenge that." Why can't it be us?

The fifth point is the most important. The Age of Reason. They call it the Age of Reason because what they're saying is that we can explain everything. You don't need to believe anymore. You can sit down and figure everything out, even if you have to invent the solution. The Age of Reason means There's no need to believe in an invisible God. The Age of Reason means there's no place for you to believe in something you can't see. Hmm. The Age of Reason means if you can't touch it, feel it, smell it, it's not real.

The Age of Reason, and the Age of Reason is as old as the pharaohs, but we think it's new. You know, they had men called agnostics. And these men went into all this deep stuff. You know, the Greeks were actually known as the Age of Reason. They were the ones who sat down and tried to analyze and understand everything. I was listening to a debate on the BBC yesterday, and they had a debate about immigration.

It was a very important debate they had, and they were trying to deal with what to do about people who move from one country to another and bring their culture with them. They had two groups debating about it, and interestingly, it was held in Greece. In Athens, where democracy was born. And Greece is now in a sorry state. That means they're bankrupt. And most of the brightest people are leaving their country because they can't find jobs. So there's a brain drain going on.

In Greece right now, these people are moving to Europe because they are part of the European community. And what other countries are saying is, "Do n't come to our country." So now they have what they call the rise of fascism, which was Hitler, and they call it nationalism, which says, "We don't want you in our country because you will make us poor." So there is this ongoing tension in Europe right now. And believe me, this will happen in the Caribbean as well.

In fact, we have some issues that we don't acknowledge, which are related to the tension in our society right now, because we have groups that have been here a long time and others that are coming, and they are starting to feel tense. And I was sitting there listening to this program, watching and listening to the speakers, some of whom were members of parliament. Some of them were, you know, heads of major organizations. And they all finished the debate without a solution.

And I sat there and said, "They are trying to come up with solutions rationally—in the center of reason, Athens—for problems they cannot solve. How can we put our trust in the people who invented democracy and it hasn't worked for them? Perhaps we need to question democracy. Because think about democracy. Democracy as a rational construct, if you think about The thing is, it can't work without God. Because democracy makes man a god. Man decides what's acceptable by voting.

Never believe, and I say this openly, that the voice of the people is the voice of God. That's not biblically sound. In fact, in many cases, God has sided with the minority. Yes, sir. Joshua said to all the people, "I set before you today life and death." He said, " And now I advise you to choose life." He said, " But I cannot force you to choose it." He said, " As for me and my household," that was a personal decision he made. As for me and my household, he says, "We—I don't know about you— will serve the Lord."

You'll have to get to that point very soon. Because the currents are pushing against you. You're 48 years old. You're not married. And a girl is winking at you, and you're a girl. Oh yes. I mean, what are you going to do with that approach? It's the other way around too. For men, what are you going to do? Let me tell you, my friends, that we're in a period of life where you're going to have to figure out where the The rock amidst all this convergence. I must find a rock.

I must find something to anchor myself to because this current will destroy me. It will pull me in if I do n't have a rock. Jesus never said of himself that he was an anchor. He said, "I am the rock, and on this rock, as the Christ, I will build my people." My prayer is that we leave this place thinking, I look at the Philippines. I weep for the Philippines to see liberalism taking root there. I weep for America, which has lost all its foundational rocks.

Canada has lost almost all of them, and there doesn't seem to be any rock left in England. There isn't one anymore. You know what I've discovered? They come to your countries and take your rocks. They tell you to go with the flow. And when you tell them you have a rock, they say you're not keeping up with the times and they tell you that you can't be with us unless you get rid of your rock. I know this pressure. But let's remember this, okay? No one ever remembers you for what you compromised for.

People always remember you for what you stood for. Stand firm. For something. The last one sums it all up. We are in the age of human society. Humanity is ancient. Don't let anyone dazzle you with humanity. Humanity is as old as Pharaoh. The Pharaohs, the Pharaohs, believed they were the sons of gods, which meant that as humans they believed they were gods. That's why you couldn't challenge Pharaoh. Some of you are wondering why Moses had a problem with Pharaoh. Pharaoh was puzzled by Moses.

When Moses came to Pharaoh, Moses had grown up with Pharaoh. He had grown up in the palaces. The man knew their convictions and their belief system. He knew their reasons and their logic. But Moses had to be taken outside of that system for 40 years. And when he met God in the burning bush, God sent him to tell Pharaoh, "You are not a god." Pharaoh was shocked. " What do you mean I'm not a god?" That's right.

And Moses says, " Look, I suggest you submit to my suggestions and release the people because you are about to reveal your lack of divinity." And Pharaoh, like most politicians, decides: "I do n't care." That's what I learned at the University of Egypt. I received a degree in the philosophical conviction that I am a god. And Pharaoh refused. And there are many today who stand firm in their refusal. Somehow, they take pride in not believing in God, as if they need an award. You are as old as Pharaoh, and he is dead.

Humanity is when responsibility ends with the individual. When a person says, "What is true is what I say is true." Which means that no human being has the right to judge another human being. Humanity says mind your own business. Humanity says don't interfere in my affairs. Humanity says leave me to my own convictions. Mind your own business. Don't try to convince me of anything. Humanity says we are the end of ourselves. Let me tell you something. If you are a god, I certainly don't want to worship you.

You can't even get married. You can't even keep your marriage. You can't even pay your bills. You're not even sure of your sexuality. How can you be a god when you're confused about what you can see? Listen, these are just questions I'm asking. You have to deal with this when you walk out that door. Humanity. Jesus said: " There is a way that seems straight to man." But its end is death.” Jesus said, “John, I am the vine.” And you are the branches.

If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you want in life, and it will be done for you. Because without me, he says, you can't do anything. Then he says, "Only a fool says in his heart, 'There is no God.'" You don't need to call atheists stupid. God did it himself. You can remind them of what he said, but they shouldn't feel insulted. You are simply repeating what others have concluded about them. I can quote God's words: "O ignorant one." This is simple. Don't be angry with me.

But as you can see, the issue is as follows. Humanity is very dangerous because this is exactly the reason for Lucifer's downfall. Lucifer fell because of self-worship. Yes, sir. Yes, sir. The essence of his corruption was when he thought he could be a god. Who are we? I am very afraid of trusting myself. I am very happy that I can trust in God. And those of you who think you are very clever and intellectually advanced, be honest with me. At 2 AM, before you go to sleep, tell me what you are thinking.

You know what you're thinking that day. I know what you're thinking. She looks up at the ceiling and says, "Oh my God, I hope I'm right." Because you know you can't be completely confident. That's why you need to live by faith, not by sight. Because your mind is so limited that it cannot even calculate what happens when you lose your shoe. You cannot find it. Lord, how can you trust yourself in your life? Humanity. That is why we must be careful in defining society first. That's what I do first.

I am trying to make you understand the community we work with. We work with a strange community. It's getting worse. Some of our people who went to university came back thinking they were smart now. They no longer eat oysters and coconuts and think they have grasped the truth. I remind them that it is better for you to be humble and quiet. Your grandmother raised you, paid your bills, clothed you, and went to church. Now, who do you think you are? You don't want to go and worship God.

Your grandmother used her feet to bless you. It is better for you to raise your hands and praise God and repent, for this is the faith we have. Oh, hallelujah. Some of your grandmothers would turn over in their graves to hear some of the things you say. Let me leave you with this idea. Write this down. We are witnessing a change. That's what we do. This change is very obvious. For example, the collapse of governments. I'm talking about the collapse of governments.

Did you know that two weeks ago an entire government resigned? Were you, I was sitting there thinking, wait a minute, the entire government? Yes, the entire government said we cannot solve the problem. Therefore, they resigned. Government collapse. Then we face another problem, which is the rise of people power, where people take control of governments and expel them from their offices. Then we witness this change called international and domestic terrorism.

There was a time when terrorists were imported, but now you're not sure who the terrorist is. This is a change, isn't it? How do you fight an enemy who is like you and lives in your society? What do you do? It is better for you to walk with faith, not with bombs. Another change is what they call failed states, which means the collapse of economies. This means that global economic security has been removed from the equation. No one can predict anything.

I assure you, it is unbelievable to hear the government say that the economic crisis is over. I do n't know where they got that memo from. But it doesn't end until God says it's over. Then we have the unemployment change. Unemployment is a huge problem now throughout Europe, the Caribbean, and the United States.
